maze_standard_budget.description: Online planning on hidden poor-localisation mazes at the standard per-step CPU planning budget (8 calibration units per primitive step).
maze_standard_budget.notes: Scaled stand-in for the paper's 3D Maze with Poor Localisation: 2D closed mazes (44x30) with two equally likely starts, landmark-only localisation, danger zones (-500), two goal regions (+2000), -5 per step, gamma 0.99, motion noise covariance 0.02*I, open-loop macro actions of at most 10 steps, 200-step horizon. Layouts are procedurally generated; the test uses 200 hidden layouts (eval/test/instances.json), train 100 public ones. The evaluator runs each agent online and enforces a CPU planning budget instead of the paper's wall-clock time per decision. Reference rows hold the paper's success rates for the analogous planning budget; returns are not on this maze's scale and stay in _paper_3d_maze / _paper_hems. Standard budget is compared with the paper's larger planning times (PORPP at 10 s per decision; baselines at 10 s). Baseline rows carry no target values: absolute baseline success is environment-specific in the paper itself (RefPol 29% in the 3D maze vs 0% in HEMS; POMCP 13% vs 0%), so the paper's baseline rates are kept only for reference under _paper_baseline_success_not_on_this_scale and in _paper_tables_full.

success_rate.description: Fraction of evaluation episodes in which the robot reached a goal region within the horizon (evaluator-computed from its own rollouts; failed/over-budget episodes count as unsuccessful).

mean_return.description: Mean discounted return (gamma 0.99; +2000 goal, -500 danger, -5 per step) over evaluation episodes, computed by the evaluator. Range [-500, 2000); failed episodes count as -500.

collision_rate.description: Fraction of evaluation episodes that ended in a danger zone (safety constraint); failed/over-budget episodes count as collisions.

maze_tight_budget.description: The same hidden mazes at a tight per-step CPU planning budget (1.6 calibration units per primitive step), the anytime regime where the paper's method is weakest.
maze_tight_budget.notes: Scaled stand-in for the paper's 3D Maze with Poor Localisation: 2D closed mazes (44x30) with two equally likely starts, landmark-only localisation, danger zones (-500), two goal regions (+2000), -5 per step, gamma 0.99, motion noise covariance 0.02*I, open-loop macro actions of at most 10 steps, 200-step horizon. Layouts are procedurally generated; the test uses 200 hidden layouts (eval/test/instances.json), train 100 public ones. The evaluator runs each agent online and enforces a CPU planning budget instead of the paper's wall-clock time per decision. Reference rows hold the paper's success rates for the analogous planning budget; returns are not on this maze's scale and stay in _paper_3d_maze / _paper_hems. Tight budget is compared with the paper's smallest planning times (PORPP at 1 s; POMCP at 2 s, its smallest reported). Baseline rows carry no target values: absolute baseline success is environment-specific in the paper itself (RefPol 29% in the 3D maze vs 0% in HEMS; POMCP 13% vs 0%), so the paper's baseline rates are kept only for reference under _paper_baseline_success_not_on_this_scale and in _paper_tables_full.

_paper_3d_maze.description: Original 3D maze with poor localization, 100 runs, maximum macro action length 10 (Table 1).

success_rate.description: Fraction of evaluation episodes that reached the goal.

mean_total_reward.description: Average discounted return across evaluation episodes.

_paper_hems.description: Original HEMS mission with evolving no-fly zones, 100 runs, maximum macro action length 15 (Table 2).

success_rate.description: Fraction of evaluation missions that completed successfully.

mean_total_reward.description: Average discounted mission return across evaluation episodes.

_paper_tables_full.format: [success_rate, mean_total_reward, reward_std_error] per planning time per decision; 100 runs each
